title: Staphylococcus Versus Streptococcus: Laboratory Differentiation
subject: Microbiology
preview: Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci often in clusters and generally catalase positive.
quickRevision: Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci often in clusters and generally catalase positive.
Coagulase testing helps differentiate Staphylococcus aureus from most other common staphylococci.
Hemolysis, antigen tests, culture and modern laboratory identification provide additional classification.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Staphylococci are Gram-positive cocci often in clusters and generally catalase positive.
Streptococci are typically catalase negative and often appear in chains or pairs.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Coagulase testing helps differentiate Staphylococcus aureus from most other common staphylococci.
Hemolysis, antigen tests, culture and modern laboratory identification provide additional classification.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: Catalase: Staphylococci are typically positive; streptococci are typically negative.
Use additional validated testing because single test results may be misleading.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Do not determine species from Gram stain arrangement alone.

quiz.question: Which enzyme test typically separates staphylococci from streptococci?
quiz.explanation: Catalase: Staphylococci are typically positive; streptococci are typically negative.
